subsystems.name: The black hole itself
subsystems.role: the power source — a rapidly spinning black hole that drags spacetime around with it. Its rotational energy is vast, enormously more than a star releases in its lifetime.
parts: ergosphere (where spacetime is dragged so strongly nothing can stay still)

subsystems.name: Magnetic flux circuit
subsystems.role: the Blandford–Znajek route: magnetic field lines threading the horizon turn black hole rotation into an outward flow of electromagnetic energy — the process thought to drive astrophysical jets.
parts: large-scale magnetic field anchored in surrounding plasma
currents flowing through the horizon region

subsystems.name: Ergosphere injection rig
subsystems.role: the Penrose route: machinery that launches matter or fields into the ergosphere on trajectories that split, with one fragment falling in and one escaping with extra energy.
parts: disposal of the infalling negative-energy fragment

subsystems.name: Energy collection
subsystems.role: capture the outgoing electromagnetic flux, or the escaping fragments of a Penrose process, well outside the horizon.

subsystems.name: Station and support infrastructure
subsystems.role: a platform able to work near the horizon under extreme radiation, tidal stress and relativistic time dilation.

subsystems.name: Transmission
subsystems.role: move power from the black hole to wherever it is actually used, across light-years.

buildSteps.title: Find a suitable black hole
buildSteps.detail: You need an isolated, rapidly spinning, stellar-mass black hole with a stable environment. Known ones are thousands of light-years away and most are stripping gas from a companion star, which would wreck any nearby equipment.

buildSteps.title: Build a station at a safe radius
buildSteps.detail: Infrastructure is placed in a stable orbit outside the ergosphere, shielded from radiation and held against tidal forces that stretch anything close to the hole.

buildSteps.title: Seed a magnetic flux tube
buildSteps.detail: For the electromagnetic route, plasma is fed in to build and anchor a large-scale magnetic field threading the ergosphere, completing a circuit in which the hole's rotation drives a current.

buildSteps.title: Or run the ergosphere split
buildSteps.detail: For the Penrose route, matter or waves are launched on carefully timed paths into the ergosphere so that one part drops in with negative energy and another escapes carrying a surplus.

buildSteps.title: Collect the output
buildSteps.detail: Structures placed far from the horizon capture the outward electromagnetic flux, or the energetic escaping fragments, and convert them into heat or electricity.

buildSteps.title: Transmit across interstellar space
buildSteps.detail: Power is beamed or relayed towards its point of use; spreading losses over such distances mean the receiver must be enormous or the power must be relayed repeatedly.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: The field, the orbit and the injection timing must be sustained for very long periods, with clocks near the hole running at a different rate from clocks at the destination.

prerequisites.tech: Observational proof that black holes power things
prerequisites.why: jets from accreting black holes match magnetically driven models, but nobody has directly measured rotational energy being extracted.

prerequisites.tech: Creating and steering magnetic fields at horizon scale
prerequisites.why: you would need to thread the ergosphere with an enormous, stable field and keep its geometry right for the lifetime of the plant.
the nearest stellar-mass black holes are thousands of light-years away, so nothing can currently be sent there.

prerequisites.tech: Materials and machines surviving the environment
prerequisites.why: radiation, tidal stress and time dilation near a black hole are far beyond any engineered system.
delivering the energy to a user over light-years, without crippling losses, has no demonstrated method.

pathway.milestone: theory only: the Penrose process (1969) and the Blandford–Znajek mechanism (1977) are worked out mathematically; black holes themselves are observed as shadows and mergers
pathway.unlocks: confidence that black holes and their spin are real, but no way to harness them.

pathway.milestone: astrophysical tests decide whether jets really draw on black hole spin
pathway.unlocks: a clearer physical picture, still purely observational.

pathway.milestone: laboratory analogues (rotating fluids, optical media, superconducting circuits) reproduce features of the ergosphere
any practical version would first require interstellar transport and transmission
pathway.unlocks: stellar-scale energy from a single object — a prospect with no credible route from today's technology.
